title: On-call Incident Communications Playbook (draft)
content:
Purpose:
This playbook collects short, reusable communication templates and a tight war-room checklist for on-call engineers and incident commanders. Goal: get clear, consistent external and internal messages out in the first 15–30 minutes and ensure triage work and handoffs are repeatable. This is a working draft — please add examples you used that helped reduce noise or cut customer confusion.

Scope and audience:
- Audience: on-call engineers, incident commanders (IC), customer success, support leads, comms.
- Scope: initial status-page updates, customer-facing snippets (email/slack), internal war-room checklist and minimum telemetry to gather. Not a full postmortem template (see linked artifacts).

Key principles (short):
- Speed > polish for initial message; be honest and set expectations.
- Single source of truth: linked status page URL.
- Include what we know, what we don’t know, and the next update ETA.
- Differentiate internal instructions (actions) from customer text (explanatory).

Incident metadata template (use for every incident):
- Incident ID: {{INCIDENT_ID}}
- Start time (UTC): {{START_TS}}
- Affected surface: (hosted-api | dedicated | private)
- Severity: sev1 | sev2 | sev3
- IC: {{IC_NAME}} (contact: @slack)
- Communication lead: {{COMM_LEAD}}
- Status page: {{STATUS_PAGE_URL}}

Status page first-notice (15 min) — short and machine-friendly:
Title: Degraded responses for Redwood Hosted API ({{AFFECTED_REGION}})
Body: We are investigating elevated error rates and increased latency affecting text generation in {{AFFECTED_REGION}}. Customers may see failed requests and delayed responses. Our team has identified the impacted service and is actively investigating. We will post an update by {{ETA_15}} or earlier.
Impact: Partial outage for text generation endpoints for some customers.
Workaround: Retry after 15–30s; switch to dedicated/reserved routes if configured.
ETA for next update: {{ETA_15}}

Status page ongoing-update (30/60/90 min) — expand each time:
- 30 min: What changed — summary of findings so far, e.g., "root cause narrowing: autoscaler failure causing GPU pool exhaustion in eu-west-1"; actions underway, e.g., "manual capacity allocation and rolling restart initiated"; updated ETA.
- 60 min: Progress and measurable signal: "error rate down from 12% to 3% after restart of 5/12 nodes; latency 95th decreased from 1.8s to 600ms".
- 90+ min: If mitigated, provide time of mitigation and next steps (postmortem). If not mitigated, include escalation and fallback options.

Customer-facing email template (short form) — use for top customers or when support tickets escalate:
Subject: Incident {{INCIDENT_ID}} — Redwood API disruption in {{AFFECTED_REGION}}
Hi {{CUSTOMER_NAME}},
We’re investigating an issue impacting Redwood API responses in {{AFFECTED_REGION}}. Some requests are failing or delayed. Our engineers are actively working on a fix and we’ll update you by {{ETA_30}}.
If you rely on Dedicated/Private deployments, please contact your CSM for immediate assistance.
We apologize for the disruption — we’ll share a full summary after recovery.
Regards,
Redwood Inference Site Reliability Team

Slack / In-app short status (for public-facing support channel):
[INCIDENT {{INCIDENT_ID}}] Investigating: Elevated error rates for text generation in {{AFFECTED_REGION}}. See status page: {{STATUS_PAGE_URL}}. Next update: {{ETA_15}}

Internal war-room checklist (first 30 minutes) — actionable steps for IC and on-call:
1) Set up the channel: Create or confirm #inc-{{INCIDENT_ID}} on Slack. Invite IC, comm lead, owner, support, infra on-call.
2) Declare roles (IC, comms, infra lead, DB/infra owners). Quick roster in the channel.
3) Capture initial timeline: record first alert time, first human observable, and first mitigation attempt.
4) Attach telemetry: links to error dashboards, NGINX logs, GPU utilization, autoscaler logs, and the request sample set. Minimum required artifacts:
   - Error rate chart (last 60m) URL
   - Request traces (one example 5xx)
   - Recent deploys/rollouts (last 24h)
   - Autoscaler events/logs
5) Triage: Is this config/deploy/traffic spike/hardware? Flag immediate mitigations: scale up, roll back, or switch traffic to fallback region.
6) Customer routing: identify impacted customers (by error signature or tenant id). Notify support/CS for top 10 customers.
7) Communication cadence: publish initial status page (IC or comm lead), then updates at 15/30/60 minutes or on significant changes.
8) Metric gates for mitigation: define numeric targets to call issue mitigated (e.g., error rate < 1% and latency 95th < 700ms for 10 min).
9) Handoff plan: if > 4 hours, prepare next-shift IC and provide summary message and open tasks.

Checklist quick snippets (copy/paste friendly):
- "Initial status posted: investigating elevated error rates. ETA for update: {{ETA_15}} — status page: {{STATUS_PAGE_URL}}"
- "Mitigation in progress: manual allocation of GPU capacity initiated; expected stabilization in ~20m"
- "Service restored: error rate normalized at {{RECOVERY_TS}}; mitigation steps in progress; postmortem will follow."

When to involve legal/compliance or notify enterprise contracts:
- Any incident involving customer data exfiltration, PII exposure, or contractual SLA breach must trigger legal and CSM notification immediately. Use escalation tag: @legal @csm-leads.

Post-incident immediate tasks (within 24 hours):
- IC to collect timeline and attach to incident Jira (e.g., RED-1342).
- Comm lead to draft customer-facing summary and provide to support for review.
- Add initial root-cause hypothesis and actions to the ticket.

Suggested wording for post-recovery status page (short):
Title: Service restored — Redwood Hosted API
Body: The issue impacting text generation in {{AFFECTED_REGION}} has been mitigated at {{RECOVERY_TS}}. Root cause: premature autoscaler saturation due to an edge-case request pattern; action taken: manual capacity expansion and a temporary autoscaler configuration rollback. We are implementing a fix and will publish a full postmortem within 5 business days.

Notes / operational tips learned (from prior incidents):
- Keep the first public update minimal and timestamped — customers appreciate clear ETAs even when rough.
- Use sample customer impact counts (e.g., "~12 customers affected") only when the count is validated. Wrong numbers cause mistrust.
- For dedicated & private customers, coordinate the customer comms with the CSM before broad public emails.
- Maintain an up-to-date list of high-touch customers and assigned CSMs in a separate doc — link in the war-room channel.

Owners and maintenance:
- Playbook owner: Aisha Khan (eng-sre)
- Communication lead rotation: weekly; update roster in Confluence.
- Review cadence: quarterly or after any Sev1.

Open questions and TODOs (draft):
- Add exact sample queries to gather for embeddings-related incidents (needed).
- Finalize approved CSM wording for enterprise customers.
- Automate initial status page post from alert webhook (ops engineering task).

If you updated this doc, add a short note at the bottom with the date and what changed.

---

2025-02-18: Added customer email template and expanded triage telemetry list (collab: Liam Chen, Ravi Patel).
